title: Faithfully flat quotients of split tori over any field
statement: Let $k$ be any field [def-weil-field]. Write $\mathbf G_{m,k}=\operatorname{Spec}k[z,z^{-1}]$ with multiplication of units. A split torus is a $k$-group scheme [def-sc-group-scheme] isomorphic over $k$ to $\mathbf G_{m,k}^r$ for an integer $r\geq0$. Let $T$ be a split torus, let $Q$ be an affine $k$-group scheme of finite type [def-weil-finite-type-morphism], and let $q:T\to Q$ be a homomorphism such that $k[T]$ is a faithfully flat $k[Q]$-module through $q^*:k[Q]\to k[T]$ [def-weil-pbc-faithfully-flat-ring-map]. Here $k[X]=\Gamma(X,\mathcal O_X)$ for an affine $k$-scheme $X$. Then $Q$ is a split torus over $k$: there is an integer $t\geq0$ and an isomorphism $Q\simeq\mathbf G_{m,k}^t$ of $k$-group schemes. No perfectness or infinitude assumption is made on $k$, and no smoothness, reducedness or finiteness assumption is imposed on the scheme-theoretic kernel of $q$. Rank zero is allowed.

source.place: Theorem 12.9(b),(c), printed pp.233--234; Definition 12.14 and its following paragraph, printed p.236: a quotient of a split torus is again a split torus. Quotient maps are the faithfully flat homomorphisms (Theorem 3.34, printed p.75; Theorem 5.39 and Remark 5.42, printed p.108).

proof.text: Choose a splitting of $T$ of rank $r$ and put $A=k[Q]$, $H=k[\mathbf Z^r]$, with basis $e_m$, product $e_me_n=e_{m+n}$, coproduct $\Delta_H(e_m)=e_m\otimes e_m$, counit $\epsilon_H(e_m)=1$ and antipode $S_H(e_m)=e_{-m}$. The split case of [lem-sfb-diagonalizable-group-geometric-criteria] identifies this coordinate group with $T$. The coordinate Hopf structure on $A$ is supplied by [lem-sfb-affine-group-coordinate-hopf]. The map $i=q^*:A\to H$ is injective: apply [lem-weil-pbc-faithfully-flat-universally-injective] to the given faithfully flat map and $N=A$, and identify $A\otimes_AH$ with $H$ by $a\otimes h\mapsto i(a)h$. Moreover, pulling back the multiplication compatibility diagram of the group homomorphism $q$ gives $\Delta_H i=(i\otimes i)\Delta_A$. On functors of points $q$ is a homomorphism of groups [def-sc-group-scheme], so it also sends the identity to the identity and inverses to inverses: $q\circ e_T=e_Q$ and $q\circ\iota_T=\iota_Q\circ q$. Pulling back these two diagrams gives $\epsilon_H i=\epsilon_A$ and $S_H i=iS_A$. Let $B=i(A)\subseteq H$. It is a unital $k$-subalgebra stable under $S_H$, and for every $b\in B$ the displayed coproduct identity writes $\Delta_H(b)$ as a finite sum $\sum_j b_j\otimes b'_j$ with $b_j,b'_j\in B$.

source.place: Theorem 12.9 and Definition 12.14, pp.233--236; the injective-coordinate viewpoint is Proposition 5.43(c), p.109. Faithful-flat injectivity: Stacks Tag 05CK, algebra-lemma-faithfully-flat-universally-injective.

proof.text: For $n\in\mathbf Z^r$, define the $k$-linear coefficient functional $p_n:H\to k$ by $p_n(\sum_m c_me_m)=c_n$. The tensor universal property [def-weil-pbc-module-tensor-product] gives the linear map $1\otimes p_n:H\otimes_kH\to H$, $h\otimes h'\mapsto h\,p_n(h')$. If $b=\sum_m c_me_m\in B$, apply this map to the two expressions for $\Delta_H(b)$ in step 1. It yields $c_ne_n=\sum_j b_jp_n(b'_j)\in B$. When $c_n\ne0$, division by the nonzero scalar $c_n\in k$ gives $e_n\in B$. Consequently every element of $B$ is a finite linear combination of the individual monomials that belong to $B$. This is a coefficient calculation on finite sums and does not evaluate on $k$-rational points.

source.place: Coefficient-projection argument as in the proof of Theorem 12.12(a) => (b), p.235, applied to the coproduct of the coordinate subalgebra; agent adaptation.

proof.text: Put $L=\{m\in\mathbf Z^r:e_m\in B\}$. Since $1=e_0\in B$, $e_{m+n}=e_me_n$ and $e_{-m}=S_H(e_m)$, this is an additive subgroup of $\mathbf Z^r$. Step 2 says that $B$ is exactly the $k$-linear span of $\{e_m:m\in L\}$; these vectors are linearly independent since they are part of the defining basis of $H$. Apply [lem-weil-subgroup-finite-free-abelian-group-free] with $J=\{1,\ldots,r\}$ to choose a finite basis $\lambda_1,\ldots,\lambda_t$ of $L$, for some $t\geq0$. The bijection $\mathbf Z^t\to L$, $(a_j)\mapsto\sum_j a_j\lambda_j$, induces the $k$-linear isomorphism $\theta:k[\mathbf Z^t]\to B$ sending $e_a$ to $e_{\sum_j a_j\lambda_j}$. Its inverse sends each basis vector $e_m$ to the vector indexed by the unique basis coordinates of $m$. Addition of coordinates shows $\theta(e_ae_b)=\theta(e_a)\theta(e_b)$ and $\theta(e_0)=1$, so it is an algebra isomorphism.

source.place: Definition 12.14, p.236: split tori correspond to free finite-rank character groups; the subgroup argument underlying Theorem 12.9(b),(c), pp.233--234, is made explicit on the coordinate algebra.

proof.text: Compose $\theta$ with the inverse of $i:A\to B$ to obtain an algebra isomorphism $k[\mathbf Z^t]\simeq A$. Let $\phi=i^{-1}\theta:k[\mathbf Z^t]\to A$ and $m=\sum_ja_j\lambda_j$. By step 1, $(i\otimes i)\Delta_A(\phi(e_a))=\Delta_H(e_m)=e_m\otimes e_m=(i\otimes i)(\phi(e_a)\otimes\phi(e_a))$, $\epsilon_A(\phi(e_a))=\epsilon_H(e_m)=1$ and $i(S_A(\phi(e_a)))=S_H(e_m)=e_{-m}=i(\phi(e_{-a}))$. The map $i\otimes i:A\otimes_kA\to H\otimes_kH$ is injective: by step 3, $B$ is the span of the basis vectors $e_m$, $m\in L$, so the coefficient projection $\pi:H\to B$, $\sum_mc_me_m\mapsto\sum_{m\in L}c_me_m$, satisfies $\pi|_B=1_B$; hence, with the tensor products of linear maps of [def-weil-pbc-module-tensor-product], $(i^{-1}\pi\otimes i^{-1}\pi)(i\otimes i)=1_{A\otimes A}$. Since $i$ is injective as well, $\Delta_A(\phi(e_a))=\phi(e_a)\otimes\phi(e_a)$ and $S_A(\phi(e_a))=\phi(e_{-a})$; that is, $\phi$ sends coproduct, counit and antipode of $k[\mathbf Z^t]$ on each basis element to those of $A$, and linearity extends these equalities to all elements. Thus the isomorphism and its inverse preserve all coordinate group operations. By the contravariant affine-spectrum correspondence [def-weil-affine-spectrum], they give inverse isomorphisms of $k$-schemes respecting multiplication, unit and inverse, hence an isomorphism of $k$-group schemes $Q\simeq D_k(\mathbf Z^t)$. The split case of [lem-sfb-diagonalizable-group-geometric-criteria] identifies the latter with $\mathbf G_{m,k}^t$. For $r=0$ one has $H=k$, $B=k$ and $L=0$, so $t=0$; the same argument applies. Neither a field extension nor any property of the kernel has been used.

source.place: Theorem 12.9(a)--(c), pp.233--234; Proposition 12.3, pp.231--232, and Definition 12.14, p.236.
